new_findings_phase0.claim: The live-RLS check queued behind P0-014 would have proven nothing about tenant isolation. RLS is ENABLED on 34+ core tables but with ZERO policies (deny-by-default), and the backend connects as the DB OWNER role, which bypasses RLS entirely (no table uses FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY). The real tenant boundary is application-layer (ctx.restaurant.id / auth.tenantId), which is exactly what A5's isolation matrix tests. Recorded so no report, doc or launch checklist can cite 'RLS enabled' as evidence of a working DB-level isolation boundary.

Every live-infra claim must be cross-checked with a real query (execute_sql or an equivalent data-plane call) and the raw result recorded. Added to the known-landmines list for all agents.

decision_pending_founder.question: Production Postgres host: Supabase Pro vs Postgres inside the existing Docker stack
decision_pending_founder.option_1: Supabase Pro - no pausing, managed backups + PITR, connection strings unchanged, RLS/advisors keep working, MCP tooling keeps working. Cost: monthly USD, requires an FX payment path from Iran; data lives outside Iran (latency + jurisdiction).
decision_pending_founder.option_2: Postgres in the existing Docker stack - docker-compose.yml already ships postgres:16-alpine (:12-26) and a backup service (:137-167: BACKUP_CRON default '0 3 * * *', BACKUP_KEEP 14, BACKUP_ON_START, uploads volume tarred, optional S3 fields). No FX dependency, same host as the API (lowest latency), full control. Ops burden ours: patching, disk, monitoring, and a PROVEN restore drill become launch gates.
decision_pending_founder.ceo_recommendation: Option 2 for launch (baseline (b) already puts the API on the self-hosted stack, so option 1 would put the DB on a different continent from its only client and add an FX dependency to the critical path), with three hard conditions: (a) an executed restore drill, not a documented one; (b) off-host backup copies - the S3 fields exist but are empty; (c) uptime/disk alerting before launch. Option 1 stays the fallback if the founder does not want to own DB ops.
decision_pending_founder.founder_decision: Option 2 NOW, option 1 later if needed: launch on Postgres inside the existing Docker stack under the three hard conditions (executed restore drill, off-host backup copies, uptime/disk alerting); migrate to Supabase Pro only if the ops burden proves real. The decision is not locked, but the 'provably non-pausing' gate runs before launch either way. Supabase restore + password reset: CANCELLED - the project leaves the critical path.

founder_directive_4_2026-09-03.hard_launch_gate_added: 'Production DB tier/host is decided and provably non-pausing' is now a hard launch gate. A10 folds it into the deployment plan before any production wiring. Provable = the chosen host answers a real query after a documented idle window, with the raw result recorded.
founder_directive_4_2026-09-03.unchanged: Live drift + RLS remains the CEO's first action on the founder's written confirmation of the password reset; the order-5 queue behind P0-014 is unchanged.

consequences_of_the_decision.supabase_off_critical_path: No production Supabase project remains in the launch path. P0-014 therefore FOLDS INTO P0-017 (no production infrastructure exists): the production DB is now a service to be stood up on the same host as the API, not an external project to be un-paused.
consequences_of_the_decision.drift_and_rls_check_changes_meaning: The queued live drift + RLS check was aimed at a long-lived Supabase project that had accumulated uncommitted manual console changes (documented in api/prisma/sql/037-rls-core-tables.sql header: migration 023's claim was true on the live DB of the time but had no migration behind it). A production DB built fresh from this repo (db push -> apply-sql.sh) has zero drift BY CONSTRUCTION. So the check is now run against a CI-faithful DB built the production way, and it verifies the repo is self-sufficient - it no longer discovers hidden console edits, because the DB that held them is being abandoned.
consequences_of_the_decision.rls_portability_verified: RLS is NOT a Supabase feature here: it is declared in the repo's own SQL (api/prisma/sql/023-rls-new-tables.sql, 037-rls-core-tables.sql, 024, 029, 031, 038, 040, 050) and applied by prisma/apply-sql.sh. Moving to self-hosted Postgres loses nothing on this axis.
consequences_of_the_decision.open_item_supabase_data: Before the Supabase project is decommissioned, one pg_dump must be taken OR the founder must confirm it holds no data worth keeping. It cannot be queried while paused, so this is unknown - and 'unknown' is never reported as 'empty'.

founder_directive_5_2026-09-04.subject: P0-021 orders + Supabase decommission protocol
founder_directive_5_2026-09-04.order_1_supabase_dump: Protocol written: audit/round-19/supabase-decommission-checklist.md (D1-D7) + audit/round-19/supabase-dump-manifest.json (status NOT_TAKEN).
